events.title: Ponce de León Reaches the Bahamas on His Way to Florida
events.description: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León sighted the northern end of the Bahamas on March 27, 1513. It was the first leg of the voyage that brought the first recorded European landing in Florida.
events.significance: The voyage opened the way for Spanish exploration and colonization of Florida and the wider North American mainland.

events.title: Charles I Becomes King
events.description: Charles I took the thrones of England, Scotland and Ireland when his father, James I, died. He also claimed the title King of France.
events.significance: His reign ended in civil war and his execution in 1649, a turning point in the history of parliamentary power in Britain.

events.title: Birth of Wilhelm Röntgen
events.description: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen was born in Lennep, Prussia, now part of Remscheid, Germany. He later became a physicist.
events.significance: Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and won the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901. His work transformed medicine and science.

events.title: The Good Friday Earthquake Strikes Alaska
events.description: A magnitude 9.2 earthquake hit Southcentral Alaska, the most powerful ever recorded in North America. It killed 125 people and caused massive damage.
events.significance: The quake reshaped scientific understanding of plate tectonics and led to better tsunami warning systems and earthquake-resistant building practices.

events.title: Tenerife Airport Disaster
events.description: Two Boeing 747 airliners collided on a fog-covered runway at Los Rodeos Airport in the Canary Islands, killing 583 people.
events.significance: It remains the deadliest accident in aviation history. It led to major changes in air traffic communication and cockpit crew procedures.
